pageCache.pageTitle: Cranmer Primary School - Cranmer Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Cranmer Vision and Values
Our Core Values at Cranmer Primary School are:
Our Vision for Cranmer Primary School is encapsulated in the six aims below;
We are very proud of Cranmer’s excellent reputation for standards and behaviour in the community. High standards of courtesy, consideration for others and good behaviour are expected, and are evident to all who visit the school. Good behaviour and respect forms the foundation for the quality of relationships and learning.
The maintenance of good discipline, a pleasant environment and a well-ordered routine is vital for pupils’ academic and social development. Cranmer has a clear behaviour policy, and we are committed to ensuring that good behaviour and kindness is celebrated and rewarded. Pupils are expected to behave well on their way to and from school, and to wear the school uniform with pride.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cranmer Primary School - A Warm Welcome to our School
pageCache.text:
A Warm Welcome to our School
Thank you for visiting our school website. We hope you find it both interesting and informative. We appreciate how important it is for you to choose the right school for your child. We would be very pleased to show you around the school, as words cannot give the full picture of the school, its atmosphere and the work of the pupils and staff.
We hope you will have time to visit and see for yourself why we have a reputation as a school where pupils are happy, cared for and where there are high standards of work and behaviour.
Our aim is to work together with staff, governors, parents and children to create a great school. We have established our values statement and Golden Expectations, which are very important and underpin all that we do at Cranmer. We welcome and value your views and those of the children.
Our broad aims for the pupils at Cranmer are to provide high quality educational opportunities in order to increase their knowledge, experiences and understanding. We aim to create a school in which pupils can discover their strengths and talents, love learning and realise their potential. All this within an environment in which pupils feel valued and respected for who they are; regardless of colour, creed, race or gender.
We look forward to meeting you and to working with you in partnership for the benefit of your child’s education.
Executive Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Cranmer Primary School - Breakfast and After School Club (Gemstones)
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Club (Gemstones)
Our Gemstones Childcare Breakfast and After School club is located in the Court Building (wedge shaped structure on the field) within the main Hall. Access may be gain from the Cranmer Road entrance only.
There is a range of organised activities for the children to take part in (e.g.: physical, creative and homework)
OPENING TIMES (term time only - in line with school's term dates)Breakfast Club: 7.45am to 8.40amAfter School Club: End of the school day to 5.45 pm
COSTBreakfast Club: £8 per session, includes cereal, toast and a variety of fruit and juiceAfter School Club: Sessions up to 4.00 p.m will cost £8.00. Sessions up to 5.45 p.m will cost £20.00, this includes a light snack and a variety of fruit.
If you wish to make use of our extended services, bookings can be made via the MCAS app (My Child At School). Alternatively, you can contact us directly at extended.services@cranmer.merton.sch.uk or 07802881014 to support your enquiries.
Please click here to access instruction on how to book via MCAS.If you don't yet have access to our school communications centre, but wish to complete a registration form, please click here.
Bookings may be made on the same day, however, we do ask that forms are submitted prior to 12:00 (noon) in order for us to confirm availability and update our registers in time. An administration fee of £5.00 will be charged for any adhoc bookings made via telephone to the school office.

Governing Body Overview
The governing body is a corporate and legal body with a general responsibility for the conduct of the school with a view to promoting Cranmer’s aims and vision to create 'a community of caring, collaborative, critical and creative thinkers’ by firstly providing a broad and balanced curriculum in a safe and healthy environment, secondly, by setting appropriate targets for pupil achievement, and finally by managing the school budget.
There are currently 10 governors along with Martin Roughley as Executive Headteacher with Jane Dowek and Karen Gentry serving as Clerks to the Governors. The governing body is made up of Staff Governors, Parent Governors, Local Authority Governors and Co-Opted Governors. The full governing body meets, at least, four times a year.
Within the governing body, each governor nominates himself/herself to serve on one smaller committee of which there are two: Resources, Teaching, and Learning Committee. Each committee meets once a term. Within each committee, there is a chair, and particularly, within the Teaching and Learning committee, governors will take on specific roles eg, be designated as the Numeracy or Literacy Governor, Computing or Inclusion Governor, or have some other area of singular focus.

School Dinners
The School provides nutritious hot meals cooked onsite by Caterlink. We follow a menu that repeats every 3 weeks (see link below). Parents' must inform their choice of a school meal or a packed lunch at the start of a new school year. This choice cannot be changed until the end of each half term.
The price of a school meal for children is £2.98 per day from September 2025. However, Children in Reception, Year 1 and 2 receive the universal infant free school meal (FSM) and those in Years 3 to 6 are currently in receipt of Universal FSM thanks to the Mayor of London.
If you are in receipt of government benefits your child may be entitled to the Pupil Premium Grant. Please contact the office for further information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cranmer Primary School - Talking to Children about Acts of Terrorism
pageCache.text:
Talking to Children about Acts of Terrorism
Take time to talk about terrorist attacks.
Children look to their parents for guidance and reassurance. Even if your children are reluctant to talk about it at first, take the lead. What you say matters.
Review what they understand.
As your children continue to deal with terrorist episodes, they may have misconceptions or misunderstandings about what took place, even if they have followed the news accounts. Talk about it in terms they can understand.
Identify your children’s fears.
Children may have unrealistic fears that we do not anticipate. They might fear an attack on their home or loss of their parents. Take time to find out what your children are thinking about and reassure them.
Limit television exposure.
Television news presents highly disturbing images and victim accounts that can be too frightening for most children, particularly those under the age of 12.
Help your children express their feelings about the tragedy.
Share your feelings with your children, but set a good example by expressing your feelings in an appropriate and mature manner. Extreme expressions of anger and grief may not be helpful to your child’s sense of security and self-control.
Express anger in an appropriate manner.
It is understandable that children feel angry, but the target of that anger should be the terrorists. Discourage stereotypes and prejudice which grow so easily from hate and fear. If a British citizen commits an act of terrorism, it does not represent all British citizens.
Spend some family time in normal, reassuring activities.
Bake a cake. Go for a walk. Play a favourite game. Do something together as a family that helps your children feel comfortable and secure.

Cranmer staff and governors take very seriously their responsibility to ensure pupils’ safety and well-being. Cranmer will follow guidelines set down by the Local Authority to ensure pupils’ safety and will follow our well-established Safeguarding Children Policy, doing all we can to protect pupils, referring to and involving other agencies when this is necessary. Appropriate confidentiality will be ensured and respected throughout.

PTA
The PTA - Cranmer Parents & Teacher Association is a group of very enthusiastic people that organise fun and seasonal events at Cranmer Primary School in order to raise money. This money is then spent at Cranmer in order to give the Cranmer community more resources for the children’s playing and learning. Should you join the committee and attend meetings, you will get a chance to impact how the money could be spent. Recently we have raised money for the provision of the Hobbit houses, Parent seating, a pirate ship and a brand new sound system in the Crescent Hall.So, if you can spare as little as 30 minutes at any of our events or as much as a few days planning and organising these events, or anything in between, please come to our next or get in touch by our email below.All parents and carers are welcome to attend. We hold our meetings in the staff room in the Crescent building on the first Friday of each month after the morning drop off. Any child under school age may join the meeting with their parents/carers supervision.Please join us to find out more about what we do and how you get involved.Thank you in advance and hope to see you there.Many thanksThe PTAcranmerpta@gmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Cranmer Primary School - Reporting & Requesting Absence
pageCache.text:
Reporting Absence
On the first day of absence parents should report their child’s absence in the following ways
Via MCAS (MyChildAtSchool)
If a parent is not able to do this then they should either call the school office or send an email to office@cranmer.merton.sch.uk
By telephoning the school office on 020 8648 2621
Parents are expected to inform the school of the reason for their child’s absence giving a specific reason, and how long they are expected to be absent.
Requesting Permission for Absence
It is not advisable to take your child(ren) on leave of absence during term time as this causes disruption to their education. Schools must follow the law in this regard and may only grant leave in exceptional circumstances if certain criteria are fulfilled. Should you wish to request permission for absence during term time, please collect a Permission for Absence Request Form from the office.
